core.title: Define each feature as the smallest independently-verifiable slice of one wagon's behavior
core.given: A planner is authoring, editing or reviewing a feature within a wagon
core.when: the feature's scope, boundaries or any of its facets (shape, wagon link, feedback loop, size) are written, changed or checked
core.then: Keep the feature the smallest independently-verifiable slice of exactly one wagon's behavior: a bounded capability that is well-shaped, wagon-linked, feedback-closing and size-bounded.
prefer: Declare a URN, a status and a non-empty acceptance section on every feature (planner.feature.shape).
Link each feature to exactly one wagon (planner.feature.wagon-link).
Make the feature close the feedback loop it opens (planner.feature.feedback-loop-close-the-loop).
Keep the feature within the hard limits and the size-max rule (planner.feature.hard-limits, planner.feature.size-max-rule).
avoid: Features that cannot be verified on their own or bundle several capabilities.
Features shared across wagons or with no wagon.
Features with an empty acceptance section, missing URN or missing status.
Features that open a loop without closing it, or exceed size limits.
core.why: A stable meaning of 'feature' keeps planning slices independently verifiable and bounded; this node is an advisory semantic anchor that enforces nothing directly — its enforceable parts live in the constraint/rule nodes that require it.
evidence: No validator is bound to this node; compliance is established transitively by passing planner.feature.shape, planner.feature.wagon-link, planner.feature.feedback-loop-close-the-loop, planner.feature.hard-limits and planner.feature.size-max-rule.
Reviewer judges that the feature is a single, independently-verifiable, bounded capability of its wagon.
verification: Advisory, non-enforcing disposition: this rule is a definitional semantic anchor — a node that gives the artifact a stable meaning but is not itself bound to a validator; it is transitively protected by the enforceable constraint/rule nodes that require it. No check is bound to it and no findings are emitted from it directly.

Compliance is established transitively: the enforceable facet rules that decompose this definition (planner.feature.shape, planner.feature.wagon-link, planner.feature.feedback-loop-close-the-loop, planner.feature.hard-limits, planner.feature.size-max-rule) carry the checks; this rule itself enforces nothing.

Facet map used to judge conformance: feature -> {well-shaped, wagon-linked, feedback-closing, size-bounded}. well-shaped = declares a URN, a status and a non-empty acceptance section; wagon-linked = belongs to exactly one wagon; feedback-closing = closes the loop it opens; size-bounded = respects the hard limits and the size-max rule.

What a check does not cover: classifying an edit as a semantic split/merge/rescope, and judging whether a feature is the smallest independently-verifiable slice, are semantic (llm_judged) judgements; no detector binds this advisory anchor. Recognizing a feature-definition artifact is a profile-driven file_kind observation (the plan-artifact kinds of the profile); this rule defines no directory pattern or URN shape of its own.

values: feature facet (urn, status, acceptance section, wagon link, feedback loop, size) changed

fires: Planner creates a new feature for a wagon.
Planner splits, merges or rescopes an existing feature.
Planner edits any facet of a feature (URN, status, acceptance section, wagon link, feedback loop, size) even when its boundaries stay unchanged.
Planner edits acceptance content in a way that could leave the feature's acceptance section empty.
Planner or reviewer checks an existing or proposed feature against the meaning of 'feature'.
doesNotFire: Editing wagon-level or train-level artifacts that do not create, change or review a feature.
Coder implementing production code for an already-defined feature.

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete plan-artifact kind that constitutes a feature definition in this stack, so the rule's file_kind fact can recognize feature artifacts (bun.json recognizes a feature definition 'by path/kind of planning artifact').

neutralityNotes: This rule is a planner-method definition with no stack-mechanical content, so bunOnly is empty: every item (given/when/then, prefer/avoid, evidence, activation) is already role- and method-level. The only concrete input the core needs from a profile is feature-artifact recognition via the plan-artifact kind (roles.plan_artifact.kinds), which exists in the closed vocabulary, so proposedKeys is empty. bun.json states recognition only as 'by path/kind of planning artifact' with no directory pattern, so no layout.feature_dir requirement is claimed; and it supplies no concrete URN shape (the exact shape is owned by the feature artifact and the facet rules), so prefer[0]'s generic duty to declare a URN stays in the core without a urn.feature profile entry. Facet terms (URN, status, acceptance section, wagon link, feedback loop, size limits, size-max rule, wagon, train) are ATDD method vocabulary shared by every stack realization, not stack specifics. Sibling rule ids (planner.feature.shape, planner.feature.wagon-link, planner.feature.feedback-loop-close-the-loop, planner.feature.hard-limits, planner.feature.size-max-rule) are method-family cross-references rather than detector/validator/finding ids of this rule, and per rule.json this rule's id mapping is identity, so they are retained verbatim for resolvability. activation fact notes were dropped from the core facts schema (it has no note field); their content is preserved in classification notes and core:verification.
